messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: DIC is "Inf"
parts:
On Fri, 2017-12-08 at 08:37 -0800, Ruby Ji wrote:
> I changed the priors of fixed effects by control.fixed =
> list(prec.intercept = 0.1, prec = 0.1). However, it still gave me
> DIC=Inf. I am in a puzzle. Anyone can help?

this is like that exp(x) goes in overflow, because the variance of x
is to high (most likely). x might data or the latent field or a combination of them.
you might look at the DIC broken down on
various indexs,

result$dic

and locate where the NA is coming from.


this is more a sign that your model is not doing as well as you think. look at he marginal stdevs,
to


--
Håvard Rue
